title: Arakhin 4
description: Why the mishna must say that priests too take valuations, then a baraita that reads Leviticus 27 word by word: an unspecified valuation, limbs, the dead and the moribund, women, the repulsive, the tumtum, and a consecrated head of a slave, a donkey or a cow.
topics: 📯 Shofar, Megilla, zimmun: why each “everyone” baraita has to name the priests
🪙 Ben Bukhri and the priests’ half-shekel, and Rava’s reason the mishna says “priests”
⚖️ Abaye, Rava and Rav Ashi try three more reasons priests might have been exempt
📜 “According to your valuation”, “persons”, “then he shall be set”: one verse, many lessons
3️⃣ An unspecified valuation is three shekels; may a poor man pay less?
❓ The tumtum and the hermaphrodite: no valuation, but an assessment
🐂 The head of a slave, a donkey or a cow, consecrated or sold

a1.he: וְגוֹאֲלִין לְעוֹלָם, אֵימָא בְּמִצְוַת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה נָמֵי לָא לִיחַיְּיבוּ, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן: נְהִי דְּלֵיתַנְהוּ בְּהַשְׁמָטַת קַרְקַע בְּהַשְׁמָטַת כְּסָפִים — בְּשִׁילּוּחַ עֲבָדִים מִיהָא אִיתַנְהוּ.

a2.he: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִים בְּמִקְרָא מְגִילָּה, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא! לָא צְרִיכָא לִיבַטֵּיל עֲבוֹדָתָם, וְכִדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כֹּהֲנִים בַּעֲבוֹדָתָם, וּלְוִיִּם בְּדוּכָנָן, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַעֲמָדָן — מְבַטְּלִין עֲבוֹדָתָם וּבָאִין לִשְׁמוֹעַ מִקְרָא מְגִילָּה.

a3.he: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּזִימּוּן, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא! לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּקָאָכְלִי קׇדָשִׁים. סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: ״וְאָכְלוּ אוֹתָם אֲשֶׁר כֻּפַּר בָּהֶם״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהָא כַּפָּרָה הִיא.

a4.he: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, ״וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְהָא אִיתַנְהוּ.

a5.he: הַכֹּל מִצְטָרְפִין לְזִימּוּן, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא! לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּקָאָכְלִי כֹּהֲנִים תְּרוּמָה אוֹ קׇדָשִׁים, וְזָר קָאָכֵיל חוּלִּין.

a6.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִי בָּעֵי זָר לְמֵיכַל בַּהֲדֵי כֹּהֵן לָא מָצֵי אָכֵיל, אֵימָא לָא לִיצְטָרֵף, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: נְהִי דְּזָר בַּהֲדֵי כֹּהֵן לָא מָצֵי אָכֵיל, כֹּהֵן בַּהֲדֵי זָר מָצֵי אָכֵיל.

a7.he: הַכֹּל מַעֲרִיכִין, כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים. פְּשִׁיטָא! אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְבֶן בּוּכְרִי, דִּתְנַן: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הֵעִיד בֶּן בּוּכְרִי בְּיַבְנֶה: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁשּׁוֹקֵל אֵינוֹ חוֹטֵא.

a8.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: לֹא כֵּן, אֶלָּא כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁאֵינוֹ שׁוֹקֵל חוֹטֵא, אֶלָּא שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים דּוֹרְשִׁין מִקְרָא זֶה לְעַצְמָן: ״וְכׇל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל״.

a9.he: הוֹאִיל וְעוֹמֶר וּשְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם וְלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים שֶׁלָּנוּ הֵם, הֵיאַךְ הֵם נֶאֱכָלִין?

a10.he: וּלְבֶן בּוּכְרִי נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דִּלְכַתְּחִילָּה לָא מִיחַיְּיבִי לְאֵיתוֹיֵי, כִּי מַיְיתֵי נָמֵי — חוֹטֵא הוּא, דְּקָא מְעַיֵּיל חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה! דְּמַיְיתֵי לְהוּ וּמָסַר לַצִּבּוּר.

a11.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״וְכׇל עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ״, כׇּל דְּאִיתֵיהּ בִּשְׁקָלִים — אִיתֵיהּ בַּעֲרָכִין, וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים, הוֹאִיל וְלֵיתַנְהוּ בִּשְׁקָלִים — לֵיתַנְהוּ בַּעֲרָכִין, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a12.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הַאי ״וְכׇל עֶרְכְּךָ״, לְכׇל עֲרָכִין שֶׁאַתָּה מַעֲרִיךְ לֹא יְהוּ פְּחוּתִין מִסֶּלַע הוּא דַּאֲתָא!

a13.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״, כׇּל דְּאִיתֵיהּ בְּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן — אִיתֵיהּ בַּעֲרָכִין, וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים הוֹאִיל וְלֵיתַנְהוּ בְּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן — לֵיתַנְהוּ בַּעֲרָכִין, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a14.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, גַּבֵּי אֵיל אָשָׁם, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ יָבִיא לַה׳ אַיִל תָּמִים מִן הַצֹּאן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּכׇל דְּאִיתֵיהּ בַּעֲרָכִין אִיתֵיהּ בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם, טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס דְּלֵיתַנְהוּ בַּעֲרָכִין לֵיתַנְהוּ בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם?

a15.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא, הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן״, וְלֹא כֹּהֵן לִפְנֵי כֹּהֵן, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a16.he: ״נֶעֱרָכִין״ — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מְנוָּּול וּמוּכֵּה שְׁחִין. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי?

a17.he: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ — לְהָבִיא עֵרֶךְ סָתוּם. דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ — עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ הוּא נוֹתֵן, וְלֹא עֵרֶךְ אֵבָרִים.

a18.he: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״נְפָשׁוֹת״, נְפָשׁוֹת — וְלֹא הַמֵּת.

a19.he: אוֹצִיא אֶת הַמֵּת, וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הַגּוֹסֵס? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהֶעֱמִיד... וְהֶעֱרִיךְ״ — כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּהַעֲמָדָה, יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּהַעֲרָכָה, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּהַעֲמָדָה, אֵינוֹ בְּהַעֲרָכָה.

a20.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶחָד, אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ מֵאָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״נְפָשֹׁת״. דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״,

b1.he: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אִישׁ שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ בֵּין אִישׁ בֵּין אִשָּׁה, אִשָּׁה שֶׁהֶעֱרִיכָה אִישׁ, אִשָּׁה שֶׁהֶעֱרִיכָה אִשָּׁה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״נְפָשֹׁת״.

b2.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״ — לְרַבּוֹת מְנוָּּול וּמוּכֵּה שְׁחִין.

b3.he: שֶׁיָּכוֹל ״נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״: כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּדָמִים — יֶשְׁנוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּדָמִים — אֵינוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״נְפָשֹׁת״.

b4.he: ״וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ״ — לְרַבּוֹת טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס לְדָמִים, שֶׁיָּכוֹל: נֶדֶר ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ — כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדָמִים, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין אֵינוֹ בְּדָמִים, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ״.

b5.he: ״הַזָּכָר״ — זָכָר, וְלֹא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס. יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ בְּעֵרֶךְ אִישׁ, אֲבָל יִהְיוּ בְּעֵרֶךְ אִשָּׁה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר... וְאִם נְקֵבָה הִיא״ — זָכָר וַדַּאי, נְקֵבָה וַדָּאִית, וְלֹא טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס.

b6.he: אָמַר מָר: ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ — לְרַבּוֹת עֵרֶךְ סָתוּם. מַאי עֵרֶךְ סָתוּם?

b7.he: דְּתַנְיָא: הָאוֹמֵר ״עֵרֶךְ סָתוּם עָלַי״ נוֹתֵן כַּפָּחוֹת שֶׁבָּעֲרָכִין, וְכַמָּה פָּחוֹת שֶׁבָּעֲרָכִין? שְׁלֹשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים.

b8.he: וְאֵימָא חֲמִשִּׁים! תָּפַשְׂתָּה מְרוּבֶּה — לֹא תָּפַשְׂתָּה, תָּפַשְׂתָּה מוּעָט — תָּפַשְׂתָּה.

b9.he: וְאֵימָא שֶׁקֶל, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְכׇל עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ״! הָהוּא בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד הוּא דִּכְתִיב.

b10.he: וְאֶלָּא קָרָא לְמָה לִי? אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִידּוֹן בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד. מַאי טַעְמָא? כִּמְפָרֵשׁ דָּמֵי.

b11.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: נִידּוֹן בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד. פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא כִּמְפָרֵשׁ דָּמֵי, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.

b12.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ — עֵרֶךְ כּוּלּוֹ הוּא נוֹתֵן, וְאֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן עֵרֶךְ דְּמֵי אֵבָרִים. וְהָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ לְעֵרֶךְ סְתָם? קְרִי בֵּיהּ ״עֵרֶךְ״ ״בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״.

b13.he: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה תְּלוּיָה בּוֹ, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״, ״נְפָשֹׁת״ — וְלֹא אֶת הַמֵּת.

b15.he: אוֹצִיא אֶת הַמֵּת, וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הַגּוֹסֵס? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָעֲמִיד וְהֶעֱרִיךְ״.

b16.he: אִי הָכִי, מֵת נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִ״וְּהֶעֱמִיד וְהֶעֱרִיךְ״? הָכִי נָמֵי! וְאֶלָּא, ״נֶפֶשׁ״ ״נְפָשֹׁת״ לְמָה לִי? כִּדְבָעֵינַן לְמֵימַר קַמַּן.

b17.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר, ״נְפָשֹׁת״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ אֶחָד, אֶחָד שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ מֵאָה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״נְפָשֹׁת״.

b18.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר, ״נְפָשֹׁת״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא אִישׁ שֶׁהֶעֱרִיךְ, בֵּין אִישׁ בֵּין אִשָּׁה, אִשָּׁה שֶׁהֶעֱרִיכָה אִישׁ, וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁהֶעֱרִיכָה אִשָּׁה מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״.

b19.he: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״נְפָשֹׁת״ — לְהָבִיא מְנוָּּול וּמוּכֵּה שְׁחִין. וְהָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ לְהָנָךְ!

b20.he: הָנָךְ לָא צְרִיכִי קְרָא, מַאי טַעְמָא? כִּי שָׁקוּל הוּא, וְיָבוֹאוּ כּוּלָּם כִּי אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא, לִמְנוָּּול וּמוּכֵּה שְׁחִין הוּא דְּאִצְטְרִיךְ.

b21.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ — לְרַבּוֹת טוּמְטוּם וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס לְדָמִים. דָּמִים לְמָה לִי קְרָא? לֹא יְהֵא אֶלָּא דְּמֵי דִיקְלָא, אִילּוּ אָמַר ״דְּמֵי דִיקְלָא״ מִי לָא יָהֵיב?

b23.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: ״נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ״ כְּתִיב, כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין — נִידּוֹן בִּכְבוֹדוֹ, וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בַּעֲרָכִין — אֵינוֹ נִידּוֹן בִּכְבוֹדוֹ.

b24.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּדְלָא אִיתֵיהּ בַּעֲרָכִין, מִי נִידּוֹן בִּכְבוֹדוֹ? וְהָתַנְיָא: ״רֹאשׁ עֶבֶד זֶה הֶקְדֵּשׁ״ הוּא וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שׁוּתָּפִין בּוֹ, ״רֹאשׁ עֶבֶד מָכוּר לְךָ״ מְשַׁמְּנִין בֵּינֵיהֶם, ״רֹאשׁ חֲמוֹר זֶה הֶקְדֵּשׁ״ הוּא וְהֶקְדֵּשׁ שׁוּתָּפִין בּוֹ, ״רֹאשׁ חֲמוֹר מָכוּר לָךְ״ מְשַׁמְּנִין בֵּינֵיהֶם.

b25.he: ״רֹאשׁ פָּרָה מָכוּר לְךָ״ — לֹא מָכַר אֶלָּא רֹאשָׁהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה. וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ: ״רֹאשׁ פָּרָה הֶקְדֵּשׁ״ אֵין לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ אֶלָּא רֹאשָׁהּ. וְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּהָא מִזְדַּבַּן רֵישָׁא דְתוֹרָא בְּבֵי טַבָּחָא.

b26.he: וְהָא חֲמוֹר וּפָרָה לֵיתַנְהוּ בַּעֲרָכִין, וְאֵין נִידּוֹן בִּכְבוֹדוֹ! וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ עֶבֶד, דְּאִיתֵיהּ בַּעֲרָכִין, וְאֵין נִידּוֹן בִּכְבוֹדוֹ!

b27.he: אֶלָּא לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, הָא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת.

b28.he: בְּמַאי אוֹקֵימְתַּהּ, בְּקׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבַּח? אֵימָא סֵיפָא: וְלֹא עוֹד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ אָמַר ״רֹאשׁ פָּרָה זוֹ הֶקְדֵּשׁ״ — אֵין לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ אֶלָּא רֹאשָׁהּ. אַמַּאי? תִּפְשׁוֹט קְדוּשָּׁה בְּכוּלַּהּ! מִי לָא תַּנְיָא: הָאוֹמֵר

messages.text: 4a

Continued from 3b: a baraita taught that everyone, priests included, is obligated to sound the shofar. The Gemara suggested one might have exempted priests because they are not fully included in the mitzva of the Jubilee Year, as they may sell their fields at any time,
Gemara

and they may also redeem lands that they sold at any time, i.e., even right after selling the field, and are not bound by the halakhot of the Jubilee Year, one might say that they should also not be obligated to fulfill the mitzva of blowing the shofar on Rosh HaShana.

notes.he: אם מכרו שדה גואלין אותה מיד וישראל אינו מותר לגאול פחות מב' שנים כדכתיב במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך:
notes.en: And they redeem at any time: if they sold a field, they redeem it immediately, whereas an Israelite is not permitted to redeem it in less than two years, as it is written: “According to the number of years of the crops he shall sell to you” (Leviticus 25:15).

notes.he: וכדמפרש התם:
notes.en: And they redeem at any time: as is explained there.

messages.text: Therefore, the baraita teaches us that this is not the case. This is due to the fact that although priests are not included in the release of land, in any event they are included in the release of money and in the release of slaves in the Jubilee Year. Therefore, the priests are obligated in the sounding of the shofar on Rosh HaShana.

notes.he: כלומר בכל דין השמטת קרקעות דהא תנן מוכרין לעולם:
notes.en: Granted that they are not included in the release of land: that is, in the whole law of the release of land, for we learned: [Priests and Levites] sell at any time.

notes.he:
אם מכרו שדה גואלין אותו מיד וישראל אינו מותר לגאול פחות מב' שנים דכתיב (שם) במספר שני תבואות וגו' נהי דליתנהו בהשמטת קרקע כלומר בכל דין משפט השמטת קרקע דהא תנן ומוכרין לעולם ל"ה ובר"ה (דף כט.) לא גריס רש"י נהי דליתנהו בהשמטת קרקע משום דמשמע שאין חוזרת לכהנים ביובל והא ליתא ומיהו הכא פי' יפה וקצת קשה מה שייכי השמטת קרקע גבי יובל דהא תניא בספרי בשנת היובל הזאת זאת מוציאה עבדים (כנענים) ואין השביעית מוציאה עבדים (כנענים) ק"ו ליובל שמשמט ומה אם השביעית שאינו מוציא עבדים משמטת יובל שמוציא עבדים אינו דין שמשמט ת"ל וזה דבר השמטה שמטה משמטת ואין יובל משמט אלמא אין יובל משמט כספים ומיהו י"ל מקצת שייך השמטת כספים גבי יובל דאין שביעית נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג:
והך דאכילת קדשים משום כפרה היא דכתיב ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם וגו' מלמד שהכהנים אוכלים והבעלים מתכפרים אימא לא תיבעי זימון כו' מצטרפין אי אכלו חד כהן וחד לוי וחד ישראל כהן בהדי זר מצי אכיל מן החולין הלכך מצטרפין ל"ה. ומכאן נראה דג' בני אדם המודרים הנאה זה מזה אינן מצטרפין כיון דאין אחד מהן יכול לאכול עם חבירו ומיהו נראה דג' בני אדם המודרין אינה ראיה ברורה דשאני תרומה שאין לה היתר לזר אפי' בשאלה מה שאין במודר הנאה ובברכות (ד' מה. ד"ה אכל) הארכתי:
notes.en: And they redeem at any time: if they sold a field they redeem it immediately, whereas an Israelite is not permitted to redeem in less than two years, as it is written: “According to the number of years of the crops,” etc. Granted that they are not included in the release of land: that is, in the whole law of the release of land, for we learned: “And they sell at any time.” So far the commentary [of Rashi]. In Rosh HaShana (29a) Rashi does not have the reading “granted that they are not included in the release of land,” because it implies that [the field] does not return to the priests in the Jubilee, and that is not so; here, however, he explained it well. And it is somewhat difficult: what does the release of money have to do with the Jubilee? For it is taught in the Sifrei: “In this year of Jubilee” (Leviticus 25:13): this [year] sets slaves free, and the Sabbatical Year does not set slaves free. [One might argue] a fortiori that the Jubilee releases [debts]: if the Sabbatical Year, which does not set slaves free, releases [debts], is it not logical that the Jubilee, which does set slaves free, releases [debts]? The verse states: “And this is the manner of the release” (Deuteronomy 15:2): the Sabbatical Year releases [debts], and the Jubilee does not. Evidently the Jubilee does not release money. One can say, though, that the release of money is somewhat connected to the Jubilee, since the Sabbatical Year is in effect only when the Jubilee is in effect. [On 4a:] “And this eating of sacrificial meat is for atonement, as it is written: ‘And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made,’ etc.: this teaches that the priests eat and the owners achieve atonement; one might say no zimmun is required, etc. They join together: if one priest, one Levite and one Israelite ate, a priest can eat non-sacred food together with a non-priest; therefore they join.” So far the commentary. From here it would appear that three people who are forbidden by vow to benefit from one another do not join [for a zimmun], since none of them can eat with his fellow. Yet it seems that this is not a clear proof for three people under such a vow, since teruma is different: it has no permission for a non-priest even by asking [a Sage to release the vow], which is not so for one forbidden by vow to benefit. I discussed this at length in Berakhot (45a).

notes.he: דאיתנהו במצות דראש השנה מ"ט אע"ג דליתנהו בהשמטת קרקע איתנהו בהשמטת כספים ובשילוח עבדים בישראל:
notes.en: It teaches us: that they are included in the mitzvot of Rosh HaShana. What is the reason? Even though they are not included in the release of land, they are included in the release of money and in sending away slaves, as [other] Jews are.

messages.text: Everyone is obligated in the reading of the Megilla including priests, Levites, and Israelites.
Isn’t that obvious?
No, it is necessary to teach that they cancel their service in the Temple and come to hear the reading of the Megilla, and this is in accordance with that which Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says.

The priests at their Temple service, and the Levites on their platform in the Temple where they sang the daily psalm, and the Israelites at their non-priestly watches for the offerings of the community, all cancel their service and come to hear the reading of the Megilla.
Everyone is obligated to form a zimmun and recite Grace after Meals, including priests, Levites, and Israelites.
Isn’t that obvious?

No, it is necessary to teach this halakha in a case where the priests partake of sacrificial meat. It might enter your mind to say that since the Merciful One states in the Torah: “And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made” (Exodus 29:33), indicating that the owners of those offerings thereby achieve atonement, and therefore this consumption is an obligatory ritual act to bring about atonement, consequently, it is not considered a social meal requiring one to form a zimmun.

verse.he: וְאָכְלוּ אֹתָם אֲשֶׁר כֻּפַּר בָּהֶם לְמַלֵּא אֶת־יָדָם לְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתָם וְזָר לֹא־יֹאכַל כִּי־קֹדֶשׁ הֵם׃
verse.en: These things shall be eaten only by those for whom expiation was made with them when they were ordained and consecrated; they may not be eaten by a lay person, for they are holy.

notes.he: והך אכילת קדשים משום כפרה הוא דכתיב ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם מלמד שהכהנים אוכלין והבעלים מתכפרין (יומא סח:) אימא לא תיבעי זימון קמ"ל כו':
notes.en: And this eating of sacrificial meat is for atonement, as it is written: “And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made,” which teaches that the priests eat and the owners achieve atonement (Yoma 68b). [So] one might say it does not require a zimmun; it teaches us, etc.

messages.text: Therefore, the baraita teaches us that since the Merciful One states in the Torah: “And you shall eat, and be satisfied, and bless the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 8:10), the obligation to recite Grace after Meals is contingent upon eating and being satisfied. Since there is eating and satisfaction in the case of priests partaking of the sacrificial meat, they are obligated to form a zimmun, despite the fact that the purpose of the meal is to bring about atonement.

verse.he: וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ עַל־הָאָרֶץ הַטֹּבָה אֲשֶׁר נָתַן־לָךְ׃
verse.en: When you have eaten your fill, give thanks to the ETERNAL your God for the good land given to you.

notes.he: מלמד שהכהנים אוכלים והבעלים מתכפרים והא אכילה חובה היא ולא תיבעי [זימון] (ברכה) קמ"ל ואכלת ושבעת בשביעה תלה רחמנא והא איתנהו:
notes.en: “And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made”: this teaches that the priests eat and the owners achieve atonement. So this eating is an obligation, and it should not require a zimmun. It teaches us: “And you shall eat and be satisfied”: the Merciful One made it depend on being satisfied, and that is present here.

messages.text: Everyone joins a zimmun: Priests, Levites, and Israelites.

notes.he: אי אכיל חד כהן וחד לוי וחד ישראל. כהן בהדי זר מצי למיכל מן החולין הלכך מצטרפין:
notes.en: They join, etc.: if one priest, one Levite and one Israelite ate. A priest can eat non-sacred food together with a non-priest; therefore they join.

messages.text: Isn’t that obvious?

No, it is necessary to teach this halakha in a case where the priests are partaking of teruma, the portion of produce designated for priests, or sacrificial meat, and a non-priest is eating non-sacred food.

notes.dh: לא צריכא דקא אכלי כהנים תרומה
notes.he: תרי כהני וחד זר אכיל חולין:
notes.en: It is necessary only where the priests are eating teruma: two priests, and one non-priest eating non-sacred food.

messages.text: In such a case, it might enter your mind to say that since if the non-priest wants to eat together with the priest he cannot eat with him from the teruma, as it is forbidden to him, one could say that he cannot join with the priests for a zimmun.

Therefore, the baraita teaches us that he can join them, as although a non-priest cannot eat together with a priest from his teruma, nevertheless, a priest can eat together with a non-priest from his food. Consequently, they can join together to form a zimmun.
§ The same line of questioning applies to the mishna here: Everyone takes vows of valuation…priests, Levites, and Israelites. Isn’t that obvious?

This halakha is necessary only according to the opinion of ben Bukhri, who holds that priests are not obligated to contribute a yearly half-shekel to purchase the communal supplies. Therefore, one might have thought that they are not subject to the halakha of valuations, as will be explained below.

notes.he: בסיפא דמילתא מפרש הא דרבא:
notes.en: It is necessary only according to ben Bukhri: Rava’s statement is explained at the end of the discussion.

messages.text: Any priest who contributes the half-shekel for communal offerings is not considered a sinner, despite the fact that he is not obligated to contribute.
messages.lead: As we learned in a mishna that Rabbi Yehuda said that ben Bukhri testified before the Sages in Yavne:

notes.he: שקלים באחד באדר:
notes.en: Who contributes: the shekels [collected from] the first of Adar.

notes.he: כדמפרש לקמן דלא הוו חולין בעזרה אע"ג דלכתחילה לא מיחייב דכתיב (שמו' לח) לכל העובר על הפקודים ושבט לוי לא נפקד:
notes.en: Is not a sinner: as is explained below, that it is not [bringing] a non-sacred item into the courtyard, even though he is not obligated ab initio, as it is written: “For everyone that passed over to those who were counted” (Exodus 38:26), and the tribe of Levi was not counted.

notes.he: מביא מחצית השקל לתרומת הלשכה:
notes.en: Any priest who contributes: brings the half-shekel for the collection of the chamber.

notes.he: ואם אינו שוקל אינו חוטא שהרשות בידו:
notes.en: Is not a sinner: and if he does not contribute he is not a sinner, for the choice is his.

messages.text: @Ben Bukhri That is not the case; rather, any priest who does not contribute his half-shekel is considered a sinner, as they are obligated in this mitzva like all other Jews.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehuda added that Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said to him:
messages.quote: Any priest who contributes the half-shekel is not considered a sinner

notes.he: דדריש זה יתנו י"ב שבטים בגימטריא ז"ה וה"נ מצי למימר כל לוי שאינו שוקל אלא משום דלא מצי למימר משום שדורשין מקרא זה לעצמן:
notes.en: Any priest who does not contribute is a sinner: for he expounds “This they shall give” (Exodus 30:13): twelve tribes [shall give], as the numerical value of zeh [this] is twelve. He could equally have said: Any Levite who does not contribute [is a sinner]; but [he spoke of priests] because [of Levites] he could not say “because they interpret this verse for themselves.”

messages.text: But with regard to the priests who do not contribute the half-shekel, in order to excuse themselves from the mitzva they interpret this verse to their own advantage: “And every meal offering of the priest shall be wholly made to smoke; it shall not be eaten” (Leviticus 6:16).

verse.he: וְכׇל־מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל׃ {פ}
verse.en: So, too, every grain offering of a priest shall be a whole offering: it shall not be eaten.

notes.dh: אלא שהכהנים דורשין מקרא זה לעצמן
notes.he: להנאתן ושלא כדין:
notes.en: But the priests interpret this verse for themselves: for their own benefit, and not in accordance with the law.

notes.he: להנאת עצמן לפטור מן השקלים:
notes.en: They interpret this verse: for their own benefit, to exempt [themselves] from the shekels.

messages.text: Those priests claim as follows: Since the omer offering, the measure of barley brought as a communal offering on the sixteenth of Nisan, and the two loaves, i.e., the public offering of two loaves from the new wheat, brought on the festival of Shavuot, and the shewbread placed on the Table in the Sanctuary each Shabbat, which are all meal offerings, are ours, i.e., if we would contribute half-shekels we would have partial ownership of these communal offerings, as they are purchased with the half-shekels, how then can they be eaten? They would be regarded as priests’ meal offerings, which must be wholly burnt, in accordance with the aforementioned verse.

notes.he: שהרי מתרומת הלשכה הן באין ואם אנו שוקלין ללשכה נמצאת מנחת העומר ושתי הלחם ולחם הפנים משלנו והיאך נאכלין הכתיב לא תאכל. ולדידן לית לן הך דרשא דהאי כליל תהיה במנחת כהן גרידתא כתיב אבל במנחת צבור זיל בתר רובא:
notes.en: It is ours: for they come from the collection of the chamber, and if we contribute to the chamber, the omer meal offering, the two loaves and the shewbread turn out to be ours; how then can they be eaten? It is written: “It shall not be eaten.” But we do not accept this exposition, for “It shall be wholly made to smoke” is written about the meal offering of priests alone; with a communal meal offering, follow the majority.

notes.he: שבאין מתרומת הלשכה היאך אנו יכולין לוכל מהן]:
notes.en: They are ours: since they come from the collection of the chamber, how could we eat of them?

messages.text: But according to the opinion of ben Bukhri, as well, why is a priest who contributes a half-shekel not considered a sinner? Since he is not obligated to bring the half-shekel ab initio, when he brings the half-shekel he is also a sinner, since he is causing the bringing of a non-sacred item into the Temple courtyard.

notes.he: אמאי אמר אינו חוטא כיון דלא מחייב הא קא מעייל חולין לעזרה הנהו קרבנות הלקוחין משקליהן:
notes.en: And according to ben Bukhri [the printed text reads “ben Kovdi”]: why did he say he is not a sinner? Since he is not obligated, he is bringing a non-sacred item into the courtyard: those offerings bought with their shekels.

messages.text: The Gemara answers that the priest brings and transfers the half-shekel as a consecrated gift to the community, so it is considered part of the communal funds.

notes.he: והלכך לבן בוכרי דפטר להו לכהנים משקלים איצטריך מתני' למתני דכהן שהעריך עצמו או את אחר נותן את הערך כישראל דסד"א כו' קמ"ל (דלא גמירי):
notes.en: Who transfers it to the community, etc.: and therefore, according to ben Bukhri, who exempts priests from the shekels, the mishna was needed to teach that a priest who valuated himself or another gives the valuation like an Israelite. For it might enter your mind, etc.; it teaches us (that they are not derived [from one another]).

notes.he: להנהו שקלים מתנה לצבור הא לאו הכי לא מצו מייתו:
notes.en: That they transfer them to the community: those shekels, as a gift to the community; otherwise they could not bring them.

messages.text: The relevance of ben Bukhri’s opinion to the priests’ status with respect to valuations: according to ben Bukhri, who exempts the priests from contributing the half-shekel, it might enter your mind to say that since it is written: “And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25), perhaps this juxtaposition teaches that anyone who is included in the obligation to contribute half-shekels is included in the halakha of valuations. But with regard to these priests, since they are not included in the obligation to contribute half-shekels, they are also not included in the halakha of valuations.
messages.quote: is necessary only according to the opinion of ben Bukhri

verse.he: וְכׇל־עֶרְכְּךָ יִהְיֶה בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁקֶל׃
verse.en: All assessments shall be by the sanctuary weight, the shekel being twenty gerahs.

messages.text: Therefore, the mishna teaches us that even according to the opinion of ben Bukhri, priests are included in the halakha of valuations.

@Rava One could not have thought that this phrase: “And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25), might be coming to exempt the priests, as it comes to teach something else, namely that all valuations that you assess should not be less than the value of a sela coin. In other words, a poor person, who gives according to his means rather than the amount prescribed in the Torah, does not fulfill his obligation unless he gives at least a shekel, which is a sela coin.
messages.quote: And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary

notes.he: דעני בערכין נידון בהשג יד דכתיב (ויקרא כז) על פי אשר תשיג יד הנודר וגו' ופחות מסלע לא יתן לעולם כדאמר בפ' שני (לקמן ערכין ז:) אין בערכין פחות מסלע ומייתי טעמא מהאי קרא וכיון דלהכי אתא לא הוה ס"ד למדרש לדרשא אחריתי למפטר כהנים מערכין ומתני' לא איצטריך:
notes.en: Should not be less than a sela: for a poor person in valuations is judged by what he can afford, as it is written: “According to the means of the one who vowed” (Leviticus 27:8), etc., and he never gives less than a sela, as is said in the second chapter (below, 7b): there is no valuation of less than a sela, and the reason given there is from this verse. Since [the verse] comes for that, it would not enter one’s mind to use it for another exposition, to exempt priests from valuations, and the mishna would not have been needed.

notes.he: קרא וכל ערכך לאו להכי אתא אלא להכי אתא דכל ערכין שאתה מעריך לא יהו פחותי' משקל. שאם העריך אדם את חברו ואינו ידו משגת ליתן שקל אינו נותן כלום אבל אם לאחר מיכן העשיר ישלם ערכו משלם אבל אם משיג ליתן שקל ונתן אפי' העשיר אח"כ אינו נותן יותר:
notes.en: Abaye said to him: This verse, “And all your valuations,” does not come for this; it comes for that: that all the valuations you assess should not be less than a shekel. For if a person valuated his fellow and cannot afford to give a shekel, he gives nothing; but if he later became rich, he pays his full valuation. But if he could afford to give a shekel and gave it, then even if he became rich afterward he gives no more.

messages.text: It was necessary for the mishna to teach that priests are included in the halakha of valuation, as it might enter your mind to say: Since it is written with regard to a firstborn: “And their redemption money, from a month old you shall redeem them, shall be, according to your valuation, five shekels of silver” (Numbers 18:16), one might have said that anyone included in the mitzva of redemption of the firstborn son is included in the halakha of valuations;

verse.he: וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃
verse.en: Take as their redemption price, from the age of one month up, the money equivalent of five shekels by the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs.

notes.he: למימר כהנים דסד"א כו':
notes.en: Rather, Abaye said it was necessary: to say “priests,” for it might enter your mind, etc.

messages.text: but with regard to these priests, since they are not included in the mitzva of redemption of the firstborn son, they are also not included in the halakha of valuations. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that priests are also included in the halakha of valuations.

notes.he: כהנים נפטרו מפדיון הבן בפ"ק דבכורות (ד.) מק"ו אם פטרו את של ישראל במדבר ק"ו את של עצמן:
notes.en: Priests were exempted from redeeming the firstborn son in the first chapter of Bekhorot (4a), by an a fortiori inference: if they exempted those of the Israelites in the wilderness, all the more so their own.

messages.text: @Abaye If that is so, that one can expound the term “according to your valuation” in this manner, one could expound similarly with regard to the ram of the guilt offering brought by one who robs and then takes a false oath. As it is written with regard to that offering: “And he shall bring his guilt offering to the Lord, a ram without blemish out of the flock, according to your valuation” (Leviticus 5:25).

verse.he: וְאֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ יָבִיא לַיהֹוָה אַיִל תָּמִים מִן־הַצֹּאן בְּעֶרְכְּךָ לְאָשָׁם אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: Then [the sinner] shall bring to the priest, as a penalty to GOD, a ram without blemish from the flock, or the equivalent, as a reparation offering.

notes.he: א"ל רבא אלא מעתה גבי איל אשם [דכתיב והביא את אשמו לה' איל תמים מן הצאן בערכך כסף שקלים] הכי נמי נימא הואיל ואקיש ערכין לאשם נימא כל דאיתיה בערכין איתיה באיל אשם:
notes.en: Rava said to him: If so, with regard to the ram of the guilt offering, [as it is written: “And he shall bring his guilt offering to the Lord, a ram without blemish from the flock, according to your valuation in silver shekels”], let us likewise say: since it juxtaposed valuations to the guilt offering, anyone who is included in valuations is included in the ram of the guilt offering.

messages.text: One can argue that so too, anyone who is included in the halakha of valuations is included in the ram of the guilt offering. Therefore, a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, who are not included in the halakha of valuations, as stated in the mishna, should also not be included in the ram of the guilt offering. But that is not so, as there is no opinion that exempts them from this offering.

notes.he: והא ישראל נינהו אלא ודאי הכי לא דרשי' ואכתי מתני' למה לי למיתני כהנים ולוים וישראלים:
notes.en: So too they should not be included in the ram of the guilt offering: but they are Jews! Rather, certainly we do not expound this way; and still, why does the mishna need to teach “priests, Levites and Israelites”?

messages.text: It was necessary to teach that priests are included in the halakha of valuation because it might enter your mind to say: Since it is written concerning valuations: “But if he is too poor for your valuation, then he shall be set before the priest” (Leviticus 27:8), this indicates that a poor man is placed before the priest for valuation, but a priest is not placed before another priest for valuation. Therefore, the mishna teaches us that priests are also included in the halakha of valuations.
messages.lead: Rather, Rava said, and some say it was Rav Ashi:

verse.he: וְאִם־מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן וְהֶעֱרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן עַל־פִּי אֲשֶׁר תַּשִּׂיג יַד הַנֹּדֵר יַעֲרִיכֶנּוּ הַכֹּהֵן׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if someone cannot afford the equivalent, they shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall make an assessment; the priest shall make the assessment according to what the vower can afford.

notes.he: עני שהעריך את עצמו או את אחר:
notes.en: Then he shall be set before the priest: a poor man who valuated himself or another.

notes.he: הלכך כהן ליתיה בערכין דאי עני הוא לא קרינא ביה והעמידו לפני הכהן קמ"ל מתני':
notes.en: But not a priest before a priest: so a priest would not be included in valuations, for if he is poor, “Then he shall be set before the priest” cannot be said of him. The mishna teaches us [otherwise].

notes.he: איצטריך למיתנא כהנים דס"ד] דישראל לפני כהן משום דכתיב בפרשה דבר אל בני ישראל:
notes.en: [Rather, Rava said: It was necessary to teach “priests,” for it might enter your mind that it means] an Israelite before a priest, since it is written in the section: “Speak to the children of Israel” (Leviticus 27:2).

notes.he: דכהנים נמי בכלל ישראל:
notes.en: It teaches us: that priests too are included in “Israel.”

messages.text: § It was stated (2a) that the mishna’s statement: And everyone is valuated, serves to add that a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils are valuated in accordance with the Torah’s categories of age and sex despite their lack of market value. From where is this matter derived?

notes.he: כלומר אמר מר לעיל הכל נערכין לאתויי מנוול ומוכה שחין:
notes.en: Are valuated, to add, etc.: that is, the Master said above: Everyone is valuated, to add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.

messages.text: The verse states: “When a man shall clearly utter a vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:2). The term serves to include an unspecified valuation, as explained below.

verse.he: דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ כִּי יַפְלִא נֶדֶר בְּעֶרְכְּךָ נְפָשֹׁת לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When anyone explicitly vows to GOD the equivalent for a human being,

notes.he: לקמן מפרש וכולה ברייתא מפרש לקמן:
notes.en: An unspecified valuation: it is explained below, and the whole baraita is explained below.

notes.he: מפרש אמר מר לקמן האי וכולה ברייתא]:
notes.en: An unspecified valuation: explained [below]. [The printed text is garbled here; the editor suggests it should read: below, at “The Master said,” the whole baraita is explained.]

messages.text: Alternatively, the verse teaches that one gives the valuation of his entire self and not the valuation of his limbs. If someone vows that he will give the valuation of a limb, he is not obligated to give anything.

notes.he: אמר ערך ידי עלי לא אמר כלום דאין ערך לאיברים אבל אם אמר דמי ידי עלי נותן דמי ידו:
notes.en: The valuation of his limbs: if he said, “The valuation of my hand is upon me,” he has said nothing, for there is no valuation for limbs. But if he said, “The assessment of my hand is upon me,” he gives the value of his hand.

notes.dh: ערך כולו הוא נותן ואינו נותן ערך אברים
notes.he: דס"ד לרבויי משום דאדם יודע דאין ערך לאברים וגמר ואמר לשם כל האברים כולם קמשמע לן ועוד י"ל דסד"א הואיל [ואיתנהו] אברים (ישנו) בדמים (באברים) איתנהו [נמי] בערכין:
notes.en: He gives the valuation of all of him and does not give the valuation of limbs: [This needed a verse,] for it might enter one’s mind to include [the limb, i.e., to make him pay], because a person knows that limbs have no valuation, so he must have meant all of his limbs together. It teaches us [otherwise]. One can also say: it might enter one’s mind that since limbs are subject to assessment, they are also subject to valuation.

notes.he: היכא דאמר ערכי עלי:
notes.en: He gives the valuation of all of him: where he said, “My valuation is upon me.”

messages.text: One might have thought that I should exclude even the valuation of an item upon which the soul is dependent, without which one would die, e.g., the liver. Therefore, the verse states: “Persons [nefashot],” which teaches that if one valuated a limb upon which the soul [nefesh] is dependent, he is obligated to give the valuation of his entire self.

notes.he: שאם אמר ערך ראשי או ערך כבידי:
notes.en: On which the soul depends: if he said, “The valuation of my head” or “the valuation of my liver.”

notes.he: בנפש תלה רחמנא ואם העריך דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו נותן ערך כולו:
notes.en: The verse states: “Persons”: the Merciful One made it depend on the soul, and if he valuated a part on which the soul depends, he gives the valuation of all of him.

notes.he: כדתנן [אמר] ערך ידי וערך רגלי עלי לא אמר כלום אבל אם העריך אבר שהנשמה תלויה בו כגון ראשו או לבו חייב ליתן ערך כולו משום דכתיב בערכך נפשות:
notes.en: And he does not give the valuation of his limbs: as we learned: [If he said,] “The valuation of my hand” or “the valuation of my foot is upon me,” he has said nothing. But if he valuated a limb on which the soul depends, such as his head or his heart, he must give the valuation of all of him, because it is written: “According to your valuation of persons.”

messages.text: And from the term “persons” it further derives that one is obligated to pay the valuation only of a live person, and not the valuation of the dead. If one valuates a deceased person, his statement is of no effect.

notes.he: שאם אמר ערך מת זה עלי לא אמר כלום:
notes.en: And not the dead: if he said, “The valuation of this dead person is upon me,” he has said nothing.

notes.he: ואף על גב דאסור בהנאה מן התורה ואינו בדמים סד"א דאיתיה בערכין הואיל ואתרבי מנוול ומוכה שחין דליתיה בדמים:
notes.en: “Persons,” and not the dead: even though [a corpse] is forbidden for benefit by Torah law and has no assessed value, it might enter one’s mind that it is included in valuations, since a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils, who have no assessed value, were included.

notes.he: מעריך אתה את שנפשו בו ואי אתה מעריך את המת:
notes.en: “Persons,” and not the dead: you valuate one whose soul is in him, and you do not valuate the dead.

messages.text: Furthermore, one might have thought that I should exclude only the dead from valuation, but I should not exclude a moribund person, who is about to die but is still alive, and who is therefore included in the category of “persons.” Therefore, the verse states: “Then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him” (Leviticus 27:8).

notes.he: גבי עני שהעריך כתיב:
notes.en: Then he shall be set and he shall value: this is written about a poor man who valuated.

notes.dh: ולא אוציא את הגוסס ת"ל והעמיד והעריך
notes.he: וא"ת והא פ"ב דחולין (דף ל.) שחט בה שנים או רוב שנים ועדיין היא מפרכסת דהויא בכלל העמדה והערכה וי"ל דבהמה אית בה חיותא טפי ויכולה לעמוד והא דנקט מפרכסת משום דלא הויא נבילה נקט לה וצריך עיון דפשטיה דקרא דהעמיד והעריך גבי נודר דכתיב בההוא קרא ע"פ אשר תשיג יד הנודר יעריכנו וגוסס הוא נודר ומעריך כדתנן במס' שמחות ומנא לן לומר מוהעמיד ע"פ [דכתיב] בההוא קרא גבי מעריך לומר שלא יהא נערך:
notes.en: And I should not exclude a moribund person; the verse states: “Then he shall be set and he shall value”: And if you say: but in the second chapter of Ḥullin (30a), [an animal in which] one cut both [signs], or most of both, and it is still convulsing, is [said to be] within the category of setting and valuing! One can say that an animal has more vitality and can stand; and it mentions “convulsing” only because [then] it is not yet a carcass. And this requires examination: the plain sense of “Then he shall be set… and shall value” refers to the one who vows, for that verse says: “According to the means of the one who vowed shall [the priest] value him”; and a moribund person can vow and valuate, as we learned in tractate Semaḥot. So from where do we derive, from “Then he shall be set,” which in that verse refers to the one who valuates, that [a moribund person] is not valuated?

messages.text: This teaches that anyone who is included in the category of setting, i.e., he can stand, is included in the halakha of valuation. And anyone not included in the category of setting, who cannot stand, e.g., one who is on his deathbed, is not included in the halakha of valuation. Therefore, one who valuates a moribund individual is not obligated to pay anything.

notes.he: [וגוסס אינו בהעמדה]:
notes.en: And a moribund person is not within [the category of] setting.

messages.text: Alternatively, since the verse states: “Persons,” in the plural, it is expounded as follows: Were the verse to have written: A person, I would have derived only that this applies to one person who valuated one person. From where is it derived that even if one person valuated a hundred people, it is also an effective evaluation? The verse states: “Persons,” in the plural. This teaches that in such a case he must pay the valuation of each and every one of the hundred.

notes.he: למה נאמר שאם לא נאמר נפשות אלא נפש הייתי אומר אין לי אלא אחד שהעריך אחד כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ב׳) איש כי יפליא [נדר] בערכך נפשות דהיינו אחד שהעריך אחד:
notes.en: Alternatively, “persons”: why is it stated? For had it not said “persons” but “person,” I would say I have only one who valuated one, as it is written: “When a man shall clearly utter [a vow], according to your valuation of persons” (Leviticus 27:2), which would mean one who valuated one.

notes.he: כגון שאמר ערך פלוני ופלוני ופלוני עלי דהזכיר ערך בלשון יחיד דס"ד לא הוי ערך קמ"ל:
notes.en: From where [do we know] one who valuated a hundred: for example, he said, “The valuation of so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so is upon me,” saying “valuation” in the singular; it might enter one’s mind that it is not a valuation. It teaches us [that it is].

messages.text: Alternatively, one interprets the plural form of “persons” as follows: Were the verse to have written only: A person, one might have said that…

notes.he: למה נאמר שאם אמר נפש הייתי אומר אין לי אלא איש שהעריך בין איש ובין אשה דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ב׳) איש כי יפליא בערכך נפשות דמשמע שהאיש מעריך נפש כל שהוא:
notes.en: Another explanation of “persons”: why is it stated? For had it said “person,” I would say I have only a man who valuated, whether a man or a woman, as it is written: “When a man shall clearly utter… persons,” which implies that the man valuates any soul whatsoever.

messages.text: 4b

…I have derived only that this halakha applies in a case of a man who valuated another, whether a man or a woman, as the section begins: “When a man shall clearly utter a vow” (Leviticus 27:2). From where is it derived that the halakha of valuations also applies to a woman who valuated a man, or a woman who valuated a woman? The same verse states: “Vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation,” to include women.
Alternatively, the word “persons” serves to add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils. If one valuates such a person, he is obligated to give the set amount according to age and sex.

This derivation is necessary as one might have thought that since the verse states: “A vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:2), it is juxtaposing a person who is valuated and one who is the object of a vow. Therefore, anyone who is included in the category of assessments, i.e., one who is obligated to pay his assessment to the Temple if he takes such a vow, is also included in the category of valuations. If he vows to pay his valuation, he must pay. But anyone who is not included in the category of assessments is not included in the category of valuations.

Having no market value, these people are not subject to assessment, and are consequently also not subject to valuation. The verse, therefore, states: “Persons [nefashot],” teaching that anyone who has any amount of life [nefesh] is subject to valuation.

notes.he: דהכי משמע בערכך נפשות כל נפשות יכולות להעריך:
notes.en: “Persons”: for this is what “according to your valuation of persons” implies: all persons can be valuated.

messages.text: The apparently superfluous phrase: “Then your valuation shall be” (Leviticus 27:3), serves to include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite in the halakha of assessments, despite the fact that they are not included in the halakha of valuations. If one assesses a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, he is obligated to give that assessment.

verse.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: the following scale shall apply: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years of age, the equivalent is fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight;

notes.he: שנודרים ויכול אדם לומר דמיו עליו:
notes.en: To include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite in assessments: that they can be the object of a vow, and a person can say, “His assessment is upon me.”

messages.text: The baraita explains that one might have thought that since the verse states: “A vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation,” anyone who is included in the category of valuations is also included in the category of assessments, but anyone who is not included in the category of valuations is also not included in the category of assessments. Therefore, the verse states: “Then your valuation shall be,” to include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite in the halakha of assessment.

notes.he: כגון טומטום ואנדרוגינוס דכתיב הזכר דמשמע זכר ודאי נקבה ודאית:
notes.en: And anyone who is not included in valuations: such as a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, for “the male” is written, which implies a definite male [and] a definite female.

messages.text: This halakha, that a tumtum and a hermaphrodite are not included in valuation, is derived from the term: “The male” (Leviticus 27:3). The definite article teaches that this halakha applies specifically to a male, and not to a tumtum or a hermaphrodite.

One might have thought that a tumtum and a hermaphrodite should not be valuated by the valuation of a man, but they should be valuated by the valuation of a woman. Therefore, the verse states: “Then your valuation shall be for the male…and if it be a female” (Leviticus 27:3–4). This teaches that valuation applies only to a definite male or a definite female, but not to a tumtum or a hermaphrodite, who are categorized as neither male nor female.

verse.he: וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וְעַד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁים שָׁנָה וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ חֲמִשִּׁים שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃ וְאִם־נְקֵבָה הִוא וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁקֶל׃
verse.en: the following scale shall apply: If it is a male from twenty to sixty years of age, the equivalent is fifty shekels of silver by the sanctuary weight; if it is a female, the equivalent is thirty shekels.

notes.he: מן והיה מרבה ליה לדמים שיהא בדמים ומן ערכך הזכר ואם נקבה ממעט ליה מערכין:
notes.en: The verse states “Then shall be”: from “then shall be” it includes them in assessments, so that they are subject to assessment; and from “your valuation shall be for the male… and if it be a female” it excludes them from valuations.

messages.text: § The Master said above in the beginning of the baraita that the verse: “When a man shall clearly utter a vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:2), serves to include an unspecified valuation. What is an unspecified valuation?

One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate an unspecified valuation, without specifying any particular person, gives the amount of the smallest of the valuations. And how much is the smallest of the valuations? It is three shekels, which is the valuation of a female who is younger than five years old (Leviticus 27:6).

verse.he: וְאִם מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ וְעַד בֶּן־חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְהָיָה עֶרְכְּךָ הַזָּכָר חֲמִשָּׁה שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף וְלַנְּקֵבָה עֶרְכְּךָ שְׁלֹשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים כָּסֶף׃
verse.en: If the age is from one month to five years, the equivalent for a male is five shekels of silver, and the equivalent for a female is three shekels of silver.

notes.he: שלא אמר ערכי עלי ולא אמר ערך פלוני עלי אלא אמר הרי עלי ערך:
notes.en: An unspecified valuation: he did not say, “My valuation is upon me,” nor “The valuation of so-and-so is upon me,” but said, “A valuation is upon me.”

notes.he: דכתיב ולנקבה שלשת שקלים וזהו פחות שבערכין:
notes.en: Three shekels: as it is written: “And for the female three shekels” (Leviticus 27:6), and this is the smallest of the valuations.

notes.he: אע"ג דאמר בתוספתא דמכילתין הרי עלי ערך סתם מביא המועט וכמה (את) המועט ה' שקלים (סלעים) י"ל דהתם בסתם ערך דזכר (ונקבה) הוא:
notes.en: And how much is the smallest of the valuations? Three shekels: even though it says in the Tosefta of our tractate: “[One who says,] ‘A valuation is upon me,’ unspecified, brings the smallest. And how much is the smallest? Five sela’im,” one can say that there it means an unspecified valuation of a male.

messages.text: And why not say that one who does not specify a person should give fifty shekels, which is the largest of the valuations, that of a male between the ages of twenty and sixty (Leviticus 27:3)?

This ruling is based on the principle that if you grasped a lot you did not grasp anything, but if you grasped a little, you grasped something. In other words, if one can derive two sums from the verses, one should choose the smaller number, as it is included within the larger number and is therefore considered certain.

notes.he: דיש להקשות תפוס את המועט:
notes.en: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp: for one can object: grasp the small amount.

notes.he: דאי מקשה לך תפוס את המרובה אינו חולק על דבריך אלא מוסיף דבכלל מרובה איכא מועט:
notes.en: If you grasped a little, you grasped: for if someone objects to you, “Grasp the large amount,” he does not disagree with your words but adds to them, since the small amount is included in the large one.

notes.he: דאימא מועט:
notes.en: If you grasped a lot, you did not grasp: for one could say [grasp] the little.

notes.he: דאפי' אי איכא מאן דאמר מרובה תפשת דיש בכלל המרובה מועט ולא סתר דבריך]:
notes.en: If you grasped a little, you grasped: for even if someone says “a lot,” you have grasped [it], since the little is included in the lot, and he does not contradict your words.

messages.text: And why not say that smallest of the valuations is one shekel, as it is written: “And all your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the Sanctuary” (Leviticus 27:25)?

That verse is written with regard to affordability. If one vows to donate the valuation of a person to the Temple treasury but does not have sufficient funds to fulfill his vow, he must pay at least a shekel.

notes.he: שאם עני הוא ומך מערכך לא יעריכנו כהן בפחות משקל אבל דין ערך קצוב אין מועט מג' שקלים:
notes.en: With regard to affordability: that if he is poor and “too poor for your valuation,” the priest shall not value him at less than a shekel. But under the law of a fixed valuation, none is less than three shekels.

notes.he: [וכדאמרן] לעיל:
notes.en: It is written with regard to affordability: [as we said] above.

messages.text: But since the payment of three shekels can be derived from the principle of grasping the lesser amount, why do I need the verse “according to your valuation”?

notes.he: בערכך למאי אתא הואיל וערך סתם אינו אלא ג' שקלים בלא קרא נמי ידענא דבלא כלום לא מיפטר ובציר מהכי לא מצי יהיב דהא אין ערך קצוב נקרא בפחות מיכן:
notes.en: But the verse, “according to your valuation,” what does it come for? Since an unspecified valuation is only three shekels, even without the verse I would know that he is not exempt with nothing, and less than this he could not give, for no fixed valuation is less than this.

notes.he: כיון דמן תפשת מועט שמעינן פחות שבערכין בערכך למה לי:
notes.en: But why do I need the verse? Since from “you grasped a little” we learn [that it is] the smallest of the valuations, why do I need “according to your valuation”?

messages.text: The verse is required to teach that unlike other valuations, where a person who cannot afford the set amount can fulfill his obligation with one shekel, in the case of an unspecified valuation even a poor person’s obligation is not determined by affordability, and he must give at least three shekels.

notes.he: שאפילו אין ידו משגת לג' שקלים נותן ג' שקלים:
notes.en: That he is not judged by affordability: that even if he cannot afford three shekels, he gives three shekels.

notes.he: שאם אין לו אלא שקל שנותנהו ויהא פטור מכאן ואילך אלא חייב הוא בערך שלם משום דכמפרש שלשת שקלים דמי:
notes.en: To say that he is not judged by affordability: that if he has only a shekel, he does not give it and become exempt from then on; rather, he is obligated in the full valuation, because it is as though he specified three shekels.

messages.text: What is the reason for this?
It is because it is considered as though he explicitly vowed that he is obligated to pay three shekels. The principle of affordability applies only to the valuations fixed by the Torah.

notes.he: דכיון דאמר ערך סתם עלי ויודע הוא שזהו פחות שבערכין ג' שקלים כמאן דאמר הרי עלי ג' שקלים דמי ולא דמי לאומר ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי דהתם לא מוכחא מילתא דאין הכל יודעין את שנותיו אבל הכא דבר גלוי הוא שהרי לא תלה בשום אדם:
notes.en: It is as though he specified: since he said, “An unspecified valuation is upon me,” and he knows that the smallest of the valuations is three shekels, it is like one who said, “Three shekels are upon me.” It is not like one who says, “My valuation is upon me” or “The valuation of so-and-so is upon me,” for there the matter is not evident, since not everyone knows a person’s age; but here it is plain, for he did not attach it to any person.

notes.he: מ"ט כמפרש דמי דכיון דאמר ערך סתם עלי ויודע הוא שזהו פחות שבערכין ג' שקלים כמ"ד הרי עלי ג' שקלים ולא דמי לאומר ערך פלוני דהתם לא מוכחא מילתא דאין הכל יודעין שנותיו אבל הכא דבר גלוי הוא שהרי לא תלה בשום אדם לשון הקונטרס וקשה דהא כי אמר ערך פלוני עלי יודע הוא שאינו בן חדש וחייב ה' סלעים ונידון בהשג יד שבסלע אחד או בשנים ונראה לפרש כמפרש דמי דהוי כמו אומר בהדיא הרי עלי שלש סלעים הואיל ואמר ערך סתם דודאי אי אמר ערך פלוני בן עשרים אף על פי שיודע שיתחייב חמשים סלעים מ"מ גזירת הכתוב כיון שתלה הערך בנערך גזירת הכתוב הוא שידון בהשג יד ואינו כמו מפרש הרי עלי נ' סלעים לבדק הבית:
notes.en: To say that he is not judged by affordability: What is the reason? It is as though he specified. “Since he said, ‘An unspecified valuation is upon me,’ and he knows that the smallest of the valuations is three shekels, it is like one who said, ‘Three shekels are upon me.’ It is not like one who says, ‘The valuation of so-and-so,’ for there the matter is not evident, since not everyone knows his age; but here it is plain, for he did not attach it to any person.” So far the commentary [of Rashi]. And it is difficult: when he says, “The valuation of so-and-so is upon me,” he knows that [the person] is not [under] a month old, so he is obligated [at least] five sela’im, and yet he is judged by affordability, [paying] one sela or two. It seems [better] to explain “as though he specified” as being like one who says explicitly, “Three sela’im are upon me,” since he said an unspecified valuation. For certainly, if he said, “The valuation of so-and-so, who is twenty,” even though he knows he will be obligated fifty sela’im, nevertheless, since he attached the valuation to the one valuated, it is a decree of the Torah that he be judged by affordability; and it is not like one who specifies, “Fifty sela’im are upon me for Temple maintenance.”

messages.text: There are those who say it went the other way:
The term “according to your valuation” actually teaches that even an unspecified valuation is determined based on affordability, and a poor person fulfills his obligation by giving one shekel.

notes.he: להכי אתא קרא לומר שערך נקרא ודינו כשאר ערכין ונידון בהשג יד:
notes.en: There are those who say that Rav Naḥman said: the verse comes to say that it is called a valuation, its law is like that of other valuations, and it is judged by affordability.

notes.he: כו':
notes.en: There are those who say, etc.

messages.text: Isn’t that obvious? Why would one think that this case differs from any other valuation?

notes.he: דמ"ש משאר ערכין:
notes.en: Obvious: for how is it different from other valuations?

notes.he: דהא ערך סתם קאמר וראוי לידון בהשג יד:
notes.en: Obvious: for he said an unspecified valuation, and it is fit to be judged by affordability.

messages.text: The verse is necessary lest you say that one who obligates himself in an unspecified valuation is considered as though he articulated that he is obligated to pay three shekels, and may not pay less. Therefore, this verse teaches us that an unspecified valuation is also subject to affordability, like other valuations.

Alternatively, the term “according to your valuation” teaches that one gives the valuation of his entire self and does not give the valuation of the value of limbs. If one vows that he will give the valuation of a limb, he is not obligated to give anything.
messages.lead: § It is further stated in the baraita cited above:
messages.quote: one gives the valuation of his entire self and not the valuation of his limbs

messages.text: But you have already derived from this term: “According to your valuation,” the halakha of an unspecified valuation. How can you then derive another halakha from the same source?
Read into this term two sources, as it could have merely written: “Valuation,” and instead it wrote: “According to your valuation.”

notes.he: ערך הוה מצי למכתב והוה מייתי ערך סתם ומדכתב ערכך למדרש נמי הא:
notes.en: Read into it “valuation” and “according to your valuation”: it could have written “valuation,” and that would teach the unspecified valuation; since it wrote “according to your valuation,” this too is to be expounded.

notes.he: מיתורא בערכך דמצי למכתב ערך ומיתורא דריש ואילו ערך גופיה איצטריך:
notes.en: Read into it “valuation” and “according to your valuation”: [it is expounded] from the extra [form] “according to your valuation,” for it could have written “valuation”; it expounds from what is extra, while “valuation” itself is needed.

messages.text: One might have thought that I should exclude even the valuation of an item upon which the soul is dependent, without which one will die, e.g., the head. Therefore, the verse states: “Persons [nefashot],” which teaches that if one valuated a limb upon which the soul [nefesh] is dependent, he is obligated to give the valuation of his entire self. In addition, we derive from “persons” that one is obligated to pay only the valuation of a live person, and not the valuation of the dead.
messages.quote: an item upon which the soul is dependent

messages.text: But you have already derived from this term: “Persons [nefashot],” that one who valuates a limb upon which the soul [nefesh] is dependent is obligated to give the valuation of his entire self.
Read into the verse two derivations, as it could have merely written: Person, and instead it wrote: Persons.

Perhaps I should exclude only the dead from valuation, as they no longer possess life [nefesh], but I should not exclude a moribund person, as he is still alive. Therefore, the verse states: “Then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him” (Leviticus 27:8). This teaches that anyone included in the category of setting, i.e., who can stand, is included in the halakha of valuation. But one who is on his deathbed is not included in the halakha of valuation.
messages.quote: but I should not exclude a moribund person

messages.text: If so, let me also derive that the dead are not subject to valuation from the same verse: “Then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him,” as the dead cannot stand. Why do I need to derive this halakha from the fact that the verse wrote: “Persons,” instead of person?
So too, this is correct, i.e., the halakha with regard to the dead is derived from that same verse.
But if that is the case, why do I need the derivation based on the difference between person and “persons”?
This teaches a different halakha, as we are about to state below, i.e., to add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.

notes.he: להביא מנוול ומוכה שחין:
notes.en: As we are about to state: to include a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.

notes.he: מהו דתימא כו' כדבעינן למימר לקמן דאיצטריך למנוול ולמוכה שחין:
notes.en: Lest you say, etc.: as we are about to say below, that it is needed for a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.

messages.text: Alternatively, as the verse states: “Persons,” in the plural, it is expounded as follows. Were the verse to have written only: A person, I would have derived only that this applies to one person who valuated one person. From where is it derived that even if one person valuated a hundred people, this is also an effective evaluation? Therefore, the verse states: “Persons,” in the plural.
messages.quote: one person valuated a hundred people

messages.text: Alternatively, one can expound the plural form of “persons” as follows: Were the verse to have written only: A person, one might have said that I can derive only that this halakha applies to a man who valuates anyone, whether a man or a woman, as the section begins: “When a man clearly utters a vow” (Leviticus 27:2). From where is it derived that the halakha of valuations also applies to a woman who valuated a man, or a woman who valuated a woman? The same verse states: “Vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:2), to include women.
messages.quote: Alternatively, one interprets the plural form of “persons”

messages.text: Alternatively, the word “persons” serves to add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.
messages.quote: to add a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils

messages.text: But you have already derived the halakha of these cases, i.e., one who valuated a hundred men or a woman who valuated, from “persons.” How, then, can you derive the halakha of a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils from this same word?

notes.he: לאחד שהעריך את מאה ולאשה שהעריכה:
notes.en: But you have derived these from it: one who valuated a hundred, and a woman who valuated.

notes.he: לנפשות להנך לאין לי אלא אחד שהעריך אחד כו' ולאשה שהעריכה כו']:
notes.en: But you derived [“persons”] for these: for “I have only one who valuated one,” etc., and for a woman who valuated, etc.

messages.text: These do not require another verse. What is the reason? Each of these halakhot is equivalent to the others, i.e., each derivation from the word: Person, is equally valid. It teaches that one may valuate a limb that is vital to a person, that both men and women may take a vow of valuation, and that one may vow to give the valuation of multiple people. There is no reason to prefer one of these derivations over the others.

notes.he: אי הוה כתיב נמי נפש הוו אתו כולהו בין דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו בין אחד שהעריך מאה ובין אשה שהעריכה דנפש משמע אשה ומשמע נפשות הרבה כענין שנאמר (במדבר ל״א:ל״ה) ונפש אדם מן הנשים ששה עשר אלף ואע"ג דמחד נפש לא מצינו למדרש ג' דרשות הוו אתו כולהו דהא שקולים הן ושוות ונשמעות ממקרא זה ולא מצית לאוקמה להא דרשא טפי מהא והי מינייהו מפקת הלכך כולהו אתו מיניה ונפשות איצטריך למנוול ומוכה שחין דלא תימעטינהו מנדר בערכין:
notes.en: It is equivalent: even if “person” were written, they would all follow from it: a part on which the soul depends, one who valuated a hundred, and a woman who valuated. For “person” [nefesh] implies a woman, and implies many persons, as it says: “And persons [nefesh adam], of the women, sixteen thousand” (Numbers 31 [the count of sixteen thousand is in verse 40]). And even though from a single “person” we could not draw three expositions, they would all come, since they are equivalent and equal and all derivable from this verse; you cannot establish one exposition more than another, so which of them would you exclude? Therefore they all come from it, and “persons” is needed for a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils, so that you not exclude them from a vow of valuation.

notes.he: שוה. דכל הדרשות שוות למשמע ממקרא זה ואין לך חומר בזו יותר מזו דנימא הך קא מרבה לחודה והך שקולין הן. איכא נמי בב"ק (דף ג.) כי האי גוונא בשמעתא קמייתא:
notes.en: Equivalent [shakul]: equal. For all the expositions are equally derivable from this verse, and none has more weight than another, that we should say this one alone is included; they are equivalent. There is a similar case in Bava Kamma (3a), in the first discussion.

notes.dh: הנך לא צריכי קרא דשקול הוא
notes.he: [ויבאו כולם]. כלומר דמהיכא דילפינן דאחד מעריך [אחד] מן איש כי יפליא [בערכך] הני נמי שקולים למילף נמי (מאדם) [מאיש] דמה לי אחד שהעריך אחד או אחד שהעריך מאה. דכי היכי דאחד שהעריך אחד קדיש ערכו הכי נמי קדיש כי ערך מאה וכי היכי דאיש מעריך [איש] אף אשה מעריכה דהשווה הכתוב אשה לאיש. ודבר שהנשמה תלויה בו נפיק מנפש ומת וגוסס נפקי מוהעמיד:
notes.en: These do not need a verse, for it is equivalent [and they all come]: that is, from where we derive that one valuates [one], from “When a man shall clearly utter [according to your valuation],” these too are equivalent to be derived from “man.” For what difference is there to me between one who valuated one and one who valuated a hundred? Just as when one valuated one his valuation is consecrated, so too when he valuated a hundred. And just as a man valuates [a man], so a woman valuates, for the Torah made a woman equal to a man. A part on which the soul depends comes from “person,” and the dead and the moribund come from “then he shall be set.”

messages.text: And therefore, all of them are derived from the word: Person. When the verse, i.e., the plural term “persons,” is required, it is required only to include a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.

notes.he: אייתר ליה נפשות למנוול ומוכה שחין:
notes.en: “Persons” is left over for a repulsive man and one afflicted with boils.

messages.caption: What each phrase of Leviticus 27 teaches, as the baraita and the Gemara’s review of it settle the matter.

messages.text: § The baraita also teaches that the phrase: “Then your valuation shall be” (Leviticus 27:3), serves to include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite in the halakha of assessments, despite the fact that they are not included in the halakha of valuations.
messages.quote: to include a tumtum and a hermaphrodite in the halakha of assessments

messages.text: Why do I need a verse to include them in the halakha of assessments? Even let this be considered only like the assessment of a tree; were one to say: The assessment of that tree is incumbent upon me, is he not obligated to give its assessment?

notes.he: דאם אינו ענין לערכין דהא זכר ודאי בעינן תניהו ענין לדמים:
notes.en: For assessments: for if it is not relevant for valuations, since we need a definite male, apply it to assessments.

messages.text: The verse serves to say that a tumtum and a hermaphrodite are assessed by the significance of the body part that one specified. If one vowed to give a vital part of his body, he is not merely obligated to pay the value of that organ but must give the value of his entire body.

notes.he: שנידון כולו אחר אבר אחד שכבודו תלוי בו שאם אמר דמי ראשו עלי נותן דמי כולו:
notes.en: That he is assessed by its significance: that all of him is assessed by one limb on which his significance depends; if he said, “The assessment of my head is upon me,” he gives the assessment of all of him.

notes.he: שאם אמר נמי דמי אבר אחד עלי נידון לפי חשיבות האבר אם הוא אבר שהנשמה תלויה בו נידון לפי דמי כולו ואם לאו לא אמר כלום:
notes.en: To say that he is assessed by the significance of the limb: that if he said, “The assessment of one limb is upon me,” he is assessed according to the importance of the limb: if it is a limb on which the soul depends, he is assessed by the value of all of him; and if not, he has said nothing.

messages.text: As it might enter your mind to say that since it is written in the verse: “A vow of persons to the Lord, according to your valuation,” a person who is valuated is juxtaposed to one who is the object of a vow of assessments. Therefore, anyone who is included in the category of valuations is also included in the halakha of being assessed by the significance of the body part that he specifies.

But anyone who is not included in the category of valuations, such as a tumtum and a hermaphrodite, is not included in the halakha of being assessed by the significance of the body part that he specifies. Therefore, the verse teaches that although a tumtum and a hermaphrodite are not included in valuations, they are nevertheless included in the halakha of being assessed by the significance of the body part in question.

notes.dh: ה"ג סד"א נדר בערכך נפשות כתיב כל שישנו בערכין נידון בכבודו
notes.he: אפי' כשאמר דמי ראשי עלי וכל שאינו בערכין כשאמר דמי ראשי עלי אינו נידון בכבודו דנפשות גבי ערך כתיב קמ"ל:
notes.en: This is the reading: It might enter your mind to say: “A vow according to your valuation of persons” is written; [so] anyone who is included in valuations is assessed by its significance, even when he said, “The assessment of my head is upon me,” and anyone who is not included in valuations, when he said, “The assessment of my head is upon me,” is not assessed by its significance, since “persons” is written in connection with valuation. It teaches us [otherwise].

messages.text: @Rava And is it true that one who is not included in valuations is nevertheless assessed by the significance of the body part that he specifies? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: assessed by the significance of the body part

messages.text: If one says: The head of this slave is consecrated property, he and the Temple treasury are partners in the entire slave. Similarly, if one says to another: The head of this slave is sold to you, they appraise the slave and split the value between them.

notes.he: כמה שוה ויחלוקו דמיו. ומבעיא לי אמאי נקט התם שותפין והכא משמנין:
notes.en: They appraise between them: how much it is worth, and they divide its value. And I am uncertain why it says “partners” there and “appraise” here.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס דגבי הקדש נקט שותפות לומר שהוא והקדש חולקין דמקדיש בעין יפה מקדיש אבל גבי מכירה שייך דמשמנין לשון שומא כלומר שישומו אותו אבר שמכר לאיזה מלאכה הוא ראוי ולפי שויה יטול:
notes.en: He and the Temple are partners, etc.: the commentary explains that with consecration it speaks of partnership, to say that he and the Temple share, for one who consecrates does so generously; but with a sale “appraise” fits, a term of appraisal: that is, they appraise the limb he sold, for what work it is fit, and he takes according to its value. [Rashi on our page instead says he is unsure why the two terms differ.]

notes.he: כלומר הואיל וראשו הקדש והגוף שלו ואינו יכול לחלוק הראש מן הגוף שניהן שותפין בו ואינן יכולין למוכרו ולחלוק דמיו מפני חלק ההקדש שהרי יש בו מעילה:
notes.en: He and the Temple are partners in it: that is, since its head is consecrated and the body is his, and he cannot separate the head from the body, both are partners in it. They cannot sell it and divide its value because of the Temple’s share, for the prohibition of misusing consecrated property applies to it.

notes.he: הואיל וחולין הוא מוכרין [אותו] וחולקין דמיו או יפדה האחד חלק חברו:
notes.en: They appraise between them: since it is non-sacred, they sell [it] and divide its value, or one of them buys out his fellow’s share.

messages.text: Likewise, if one says: The head of this donkey is consecrated property, he and the Temple treasury are partners in the donkey. And if one says to another: The head of this donkey is sold to you, they appraise the donkey and split the value between them.

But if one says to another: The head of this cow is sold to you, he has sold him only the head of the cow. Moreover, even if he says: The head of this cow is consecrated property, the Temple treasury has ownership only of the cow’s head.

notes.he: הואיל ועשוי הוא למכור ראש של בהמה ולא הגוף בבית הקצבות:
notes.en: The Temple has only its head: since it is customary to sell an animal’s head, without the body, at the butcher shops.

messages.text: This difference between these cases is due to the fact that the head of an ox is sold independently in the butcher shop.

notes.he: מאי טעמא דגבי פרה לא הקדיש אלא ראשה:
notes.en: And Rav Pappa said: what is the reason that with a cow he consecrated only its head?

notes.dh: דהא מזדבן ריש תורא בבי טבחא
notes.he: אבל ראש עבד וראש חמור אין דרך למכור הלכך לפלגיה זבניה לפלגיה אקדשיה:
notes.en: Because the head of an ox is sold at the butcher’s: but it is not customary to sell the head of a slave or the head of a donkey; therefore he sold half of it, [or] consecrated half of it.

messages.caption: The baraita Abaye cites: consecrating or selling “the head” of a slave, a donkey or a cow.

messages.text: But isn’t it the halakha that a donkey and a cow are not included in valuations, and therefore are not assessed by the significance of the body part that is mentioned? If one consecrated their heads, their entire body is not consecrated.

notes.he: דקתני הוא והקדש שותפין בו ולא הוי כוליה דהקדש:
notes.en: And is not assessed by its significance: for it teaches, “He and the Temple are partners in it,” and it does not all belong to the Temple.

notes.dh: והא פרה וחמור דליתנהו בערכין ואינו נידון בכבודו
notes.he: וכל שכן כשמקדיש הגוף דפשטה קדושה בכולה:
notes.en: But a cow and a donkey, which are not included in valuations, are not assessed by its significance: and all the more so, when one consecrates the body, the sanctity spreads to all of it.

notes.he: דלא הוי כוליה הקדש אע"ג דנשמה תלויה בראש:
notes.en: And is not assessed by its significance: for it does not all become consecrated, even though the soul depends on the head.

messages.text: @Abaye And according to your reasoning, that the halakha of assessment by the significance of the specified body part is contingent on inclusion in valuations, the case of a slave should pose a difficulty for you: A slave is included in the halakha of valuations, as stated in the mishna, and yet the baraita teaches that he is not assessed by the significance of the body part that is specified.

notes.he: כדקתני במתני' וקתני בהך ברייתא גבי עבד נמי הוא והקדש שותפין בו דאין נידון בכבודו:
notes.en: But a slave, who is included in valuations: as taught in the mishna; and this baraita teaches about a slave too, “He and the Temple are partners in it,” so he is not assessed by its significance.

messages.text: Rather, this is not difficult. This baraita, which states that in the case of a slave or donkey the head alone is consecrated, is referring to items consecrated in order to purchase offerings for the altar. On the other hand, that baraita, which rules that in the case of a tumtum one must pay his entire value, is referring to items consecrated for Temple maintenance. In such a case, it is assessed by the significance of the body part that is specified. Here we follow the paradigm of valuation, whose payment is also used for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: הך ברייתא דקדשי מזבח דאמר ראש חמור או עבד זה לדמי עולה אין נידון בכבודו דכי כתיב נפשות גבי ערכין כתיב דקדשי בדק הבית נינהו וכי קאמרינן אנו דנידון בכבודו אפילו טומטום שנדר דמיו בקדשי בדק הבית:
notes.en: Rather, it is not difficult: this baraita is about items consecrated for the altar, where he said, “The head of this donkey” or “this slave is for the value of a burnt offering,” and it is not assessed by its significance, for when “persons” is written, it is written with regard to valuations, which are consecrated for Temple maintenance. And when we say that it is assessed by its significance, even a tumtum, it is where he vowed his assessment for Temple maintenance.

notes.dh: הא לא קשיא הא בקדשי מזבח הא בקדשי בדק הבית
notes.he: ברייתא בקדשי מזבח דאמר ראש חמור הקדש לדמי עולה ואינו נידון בכבודו דכי כתיב נפשות גבי ערכין כתיב דקדשי בדק הבית נינהו וכי אמרינן אנו דנידון בכבודו אפילו טומטום שנודר לדמיו לבדק הבית:
notes.en: This is not difficult: this is with items consecrated for the altar, that is with items consecrated for Temple maintenance: the baraita is about items consecrated for the altar, where he said, “The head of the donkey is consecrated for the value of a burnt offering,” and it is not assessed by its significance, for when “persons” is written it is written about valuations, which are consecrated for Temple maintenance. And when we say that it is assessed by its significance, even a tumtum, it is where he vows his assessment for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: כלומר הא דאמר שניהן שותפין דאקדשיה קדושת מזבח:
notes.en: This is with items consecrated for the altar, etc.: that is, where it says the two of them are partners, it is where he consecrated it with the sanctity of the altar.

notes.he: והא דאקדשיה בקדושת בדק הבית נידון בכבודו דהיינו דומיא דערכין דהוו קדושת בדק הבית:
notes.en: And where he consecrated it with the sanctity of Temple maintenance, it is assessed by its significance, which is like valuations, which have the sanctity of Temple maintenance.

messages.text: In what manner did you interpret the baraita that discusses consecrating the head of a slave? You interpreted it as dealing with a case of items consecrated in order to purchase offerings for the altar. But if so, say the latter clause: Moreover, even if he says: The head of this cow is consecrated property, the Temple treasury has ownership only of the cow’s head.
messages.quote: items consecrated in order to purchase offerings for the altar

messages.text: According to this interpretation, that it is referring to items consecrated for the altar, why is the head alone consecrated? Let its sanctity spread throughout the entire cow. Isn’t it taught in a baraita: In a case where one says: …

notes.he: הואיל וחזיא להקרבה:
notes.en: Let the sanctity spread through all of it: since it is fit to be sacrificed.

messages.text: The baraita the Gemara cites continues on 5a: “The leg of this animal is a burnt offering…”
